mechanism_narrative: Three consecutive weekly gains in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES show commuters and workers are returning, which will lift weekday retail-and-recreation footfall and push RETAIL_REC above its last 28-day mean over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -37.1 to -26.6 and WORKPLACES from -17.0 to -11.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue rising but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT crosses above -25.0 percent for the first time in four weeks, it signals removal of travel aversion sufficient to trigger discretionary shopping trips, raising RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -25.0 percent
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses above -25.0 and RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not exceed its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous PARKS increases and RESIDENTIAL declines indicate a shift from home confinement to outdoor activity, which will spill over into retail-and-recreation visits and lift RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -14.4 to 5.6 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 9.0 to 5.1
failure_condition: If PARKS rises while RESIDENTIAL falls and RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is not higher than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under gradual reopening, a WORKPLACES weekly mean above -15.0 for two consecutive weeks signals durable commuting resumption, which will support higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks through after-work spending.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean remains above -15.0 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays above -15.0 for two weeks and RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Seasonal spring weather drives PARKS mobility upward, and the resulting outdoor foot traffic near retail corridors will lift RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -14.4 to 5.6 in four weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS continues to rise but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days does not exceed its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent GROCERY_PHARM above +9.0 percent signals households still concentrating on essentials and avoiding discretionary retail, which will keep RETAIL_REC below its last 28-day mean over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean stays above 9.0 percent for four weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains above 9.0 and RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT recovering above -27.0 together with PARKS above +4.0 creates a joint mobility impulse that increases non-essential trips, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next week.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT is above -27.0 and PARKS above +4.0 but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not higher than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL remaining above +5.0 percent indicates continued stay-at-home behavior that suppresses retail-and-recreation trips, so RETAIL_REC will fall below its last 28-day mean over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean remains above 5.0 percent
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 9.0 to 5.1 but remains positive
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above 5.0 and RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its last 28-day mean.
